title: Advancements in dental bioreactor design for application in dentistry
author: Astudillo-Ortiz, Babo, et al.

steps.title: Prepare tooth roots and condition dentin
steps.instruction: Store six mandibular premolars in physiological saline, then prepare each root using a 1.2 mm diameter cylindrical diamond drill and apply Aksel's dentin conditioning protocol (modified) with sodium hypochlorite, milli‑Q water, EDTA, and PBS.

substeps.instruction: Store six mandibular premolars in physiological saline.
Drill each root with a 1.2 mm diameter cylindrical diamond drill.
Condition dentin using sodium hypochlorite, milli‑Q water, EDTA, and PBS according to the modified Aksel protocol.

steps.title: Synthesize aldehyde‑hydrazide HA hydrogel
steps.instruction: Dissolve aldehyde‑modified hyaluronic acid in PBS at 2 wt% and hydrazide‑modified hyaluronic acid in platelet lysate at 2 wt%, then sterilize the combined solutions by UV irradiation before cell encapsulation.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve aldehyde‑modified hyaluronic acid in PBS to a final concentration of 2 wt%.
Dissolve hydrazide‑modified hyaluronic acid in platelet lysate to a final concentration of 2 wt%.
Sterilize both solutions by UV irradiation.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension at 8×10⁶ cells/mL
steps.instruction: After reaching confluence, trypsinize dental pulp cells (DPCs), suspend them in culture media, count, centrifuge at 300 ×g for 5 min at 22 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend at ~8 × 10⁶ cells per mL in the hydrazide‑modified HA solution; blend gently with a piston pipette using up‑and‑down motions.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cells in culture media and perform cell counting.
Centrifuge the suspension at 300 ×g for 5 min at 22 °C.
Reconstitute cells at approximately 8 × 10⁶ cells/mL in the hydrazide‑modified HA solution (from step 2).
Blend the cell‑hydrogel mixture thoroughly with a piston pipette in an up‑and‑down motion.

steps.title: Load cell‑hydrogel into root canals
steps.instruction: Using a sterilized double‑barrel syringe (A and B) equipped with a static mixer and gauge needle, fill barrel A with aldehyde‑modified HA solution, barrel B with the cell‑laden hydrazide‑modified HA mixture, and dispense a 10 µL aliquot of the combined hydrogel into each prepared root canal.

substeps.instruction: Sterilize a double‑barrel syringe and label barrels A and B.
Load barrel A with the aldehyde‑modified HA solution (from step 2).
Load barrel B with the cell‑laden hydrazide‑modified HA mixture (from step 3).
Attach a static mixer at the outlet and a gauge needle to the tip.
Dispense 10 µL of the mixed hydrogel into each root canal.

steps.title: Seal pulp chambers with MTA and glass ionomer
steps.instruction: Hermetically seal each pulp chamber by applying mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA; Cerkamed) as a restorative foundation and capping it with glass ionomer cement (Vitrebond, 3 M).

substeps.instruction: Apply MTA (Cerkamed) to the pulp chamber access of each tooth.
Cap the MTA layer with glass ionomer cement (Vitrebond, 3 M) to achieve a hermetic seal.

steps.title: Place samples in bioreactor
steps.instruction: Insert the six sealed dental samples into the bioreactor, ensuring all are subjected to identical culture conditions.
